This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.
SCCH-5 2

. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 23.04.2024 at about 1.00 p.m. he had been travelling as a pillion rider on motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-EU-8009 being ridden by its rider near Krishnappanakoppalu Gate, Huliyurdurga Hobli, Kunigal Taluk, Tumkuru, at that time, a dog came infront of motor cycle, consequently the rider of the said vehicle applied sudden break and lost control over the same and fell down on the road.
Due to the said impact, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was taken to Government Hospital,
Kunigal and after firstaid he was shifted to Bowring & Lady Curzon Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and spent a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses.
SCCH-5 3.

At the time of the accident he was aged about 61 years, hale and healthy, working as agrculturist,
thereby earning Rs.30,000/- p.m., due to this accident he is not able to work as normal.
Out of this accident crime No.95/2024 is registered against the rider of the said motor cycle before the Huliyurduga Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 is the owner, respondent No.2 is insurer of the said motor cycle, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has appeared through counsel, but not chosen to file written statement.

Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement and submitted that, SCCH-5 respondent No.2 is insurer of the motor cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-06-EU-8009 and liability if any to pay the compensation is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further submitted that, he is entitled to seek protection available under Sec.147 and 149(2) of M.V.Act.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.
Further submitted that, rider of the said offending motor cycle did not possess valid and effective driving licence and said motor cycle was not having valid permit and FC as on the date of accident.

5. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, this court has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1. Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 23.04.2024 at about 1.00 p.m. near SCCH-5 Krishnappanakoppalu Gate, Huliyurdurga Hobli, Kunigal Taluk, Tumkuru due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle bearing Reg.
 No.KA-06-EU-8009 and caused  accident, as mentioned in claim  petition?
2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

6. In order to prove his case, Petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW-1, examined Medical Record Officer at Bowring & Lady Curzon Hospital as PW-2 and Dr.S.A.Somashekara, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital as PW-3 and marked 22 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.22 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, there is no evidence of respondents.
SCCH-5 7.

Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
8. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW-1, in his chief- examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of vehicle inspection report is SCCH-5 marked as Ex.P.5, copy of Sec.133 notice is marked as Ex.P.7, copy of reply notice is marked as Ex.P.8, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.9, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.10.

Further to substantiate the petitioner case, he examined MRO and Doctor as PW-2 and PW-3 and records those have marked i.e., FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, sketch, vehicle inspection report,
Sec.133 notice, reply notice, IMV Report and charge sheet corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident dated 23.04.2024 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
10.

Per contra, except appearance, filing of written statement, respondent No.2 has not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.
SCCH-5

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 23.04.2024 at about 1.00 p.m. when he was travelling as a pillion rider on motor cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-06-EU-8009 near Krishnappanakoppalu Gate, Huliyurdurga Hobli, Kunigal Taluk,
Tumkuru.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
11. On the other hand, there is no defence evidence and the police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-EU-8009.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal SCCH-5 comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the above issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.

12. Issue No.2:- As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained Type II open fracture right distal femur + right proximal tibial fracture, for the said injuries, he underwent surgery in the form of ORIF with DFLCP (9 Holed) for femur and ORIF with PTLCP (11 holed) for tibia.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.6, medical prescriptions marked as Ex.P.11, medical bills amounting to Rs.8,935/- marked as Ex.P.12, X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.14 and discharge summary marked as Ex.P.15 issued by Bowring & Lady Curzon Hospital, wherein he took treatment as indoor patient from 24.04.2024 to 10.05.2024.
SCCH-5 13

. In order to substantiate his case, he has examined Medical Record Officer at Bowring & Lady Curzon Hospital as PW-2 and exhibited authorization letter marked as Ex.P.16, copy of police intimation marked as Ex.P.17, copy of MLC Extract marked as Ex.P.18, inpatient case sheet marked as Ex.P.19 and X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.20.
14.

Further Dr.S.A.Somashekara, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital is examined as PW-3 and exhibited OPD card marked as Ex.P.21 and X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.22 and he has assessed total disability of right lower limb at 54% and whole body disability at 27%.
In cross-examination he has categorically admitted that, he has not treated the petitioner.
Further deposed that, he has examined the petitioner to assess the disability and he is not aware of having BP and sugar to the SCCH-5 petitioner.

Further deposed that, normally to the old aged person the healing time requires Ningaiah vs Kumar H H on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18960006/
4 some delay.

sentences.text: Further deposed that, fractures are uniting, but it takes some time.

Under such circumstances, considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also by relying on citation reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343 between Rajkumar V/s. Ajay Kumar, the functional disability of the petitioner is considered at the rate of 18% i.e., 1/3rd to the whole body out of 54% of right lower limb disability, for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

15. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 61 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.13, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner as 01.01.1963 and the alleged accident is occurred on SCCH-5 23.04.2024, accordingly relying on Ex.P.13 his age is considered about 62 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 7 is applicable as per decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s.
Delhi Transport Corporation and others.
16. As per his case, he was working as agriculturist, thereby earning Rs.30,000/- p.m., to prove the said fact, there are no documents on record.

Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.15,750/- p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

sentences.text: SCCH-5
It is admitted fact that, as per the discharge summary marked as Ex.P.15, petitioner was admitted in Bowring & Lady Curzon Hospital as inpatient from 24.04.2024 to 10.05.2024 i.e., for 16 days.

For the said period he is entitled for the loss of income as per the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner should be taken into consideration i.e., Rs.15,750/- p.m.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the income of said quantum for the period he was admitted as inpatient in the hospital.
So petitioner is entitled for Rs.8,400/- towards loss on income during laid up period.
SCCH-5 18
. Further admittedly petitioner has exhibited Ex.P.12 medical bills for Rs.8,935/-.
On perusal of the said bills it is clearly stated about spending of amount for this treatment is concerned.
Further on perusal of Ex.P.6 in which Doctor who have treated has categorically stated that, petitioner has sustained grievous injury out of the accident caused on 23.04.2024.

So as per Ex.P.6 wound certificate, petitioner has sustained pain and swelling in right knee, fracture in distal part of femur,
which is grievous in nature.
Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against Kumara H.H. for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337, 338 of IPC.

So the said charge sheet materials and evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 clearly states that, petitioner is suffering from grievous injury out of the accident caused in the alleged accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

20. Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-
Sl.No.
Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1. Loss of Future Income 2,38,140-00 2.
Pain and sufferings 15,000-00 3. Conveyance, nourishment and 15,000-00 attendant charges
4. Medical Expenses 8,935-00 5. Loss of amenities in life 15,000-00 6.
Loss of income during laid up 8,400-00 SCCH-5 period Total 3,00,475-00 21.
Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,00,475/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

22. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.0720013123P103400288 which is valid for the period from 30.06.2023 to 29.06.2024, the alleged accident was occurred on 23.04.2024 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Hence naturally liability of respondent No.1 shall go against respondent No.2, so that, respondent No.2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With SCCH-5 these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
23. Issue No.3:

For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER

: :
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,00,475/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Four Hundred Seventy Five Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of Ningaiah vs Kumar H H on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18960006/
6 petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept SCCH-5 in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
